A1.justification: Both complete 30-page PDFs describe the same work, Masked Diffusion Models as Energy Minimization. Text extraction and rendered-page inspection support comparison of the equations, figures, tables and Appendices A–E; the appendix pages are pixel-identical.

before.justification: v1 reports original synthetic sampling experiments and evaluations of schedule tuning on LLaDA 8B across six benchmarks, with numerical results and generated examples in Appendix E.

after.justification: v2 retains the original synthetic experiments, six-benchmark LLaDA 8B evaluations, numerical results and generated examples.

M1.justification: The Beta-CDF parameterization, optimal schedule mapping and post-training tuning procedure remain unchanged. The correction to the background flow equation matches the convention already used in v1's appendix derivations.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate MBPP, HumanEval, BBH, GSM8K, Hendrycks Math and Minerva Math, alongside the same synthetic binary-sequence distributions. No dataset, task or test scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: Corresponding comparisons retain the same linear, sine and squared-sine baselines and the same Beta-parameterized schedule variants. Comparator membership is unchanged throughout Tables 1–9 and the experimental figures.

E3.justification: The LLaDA 8B configuration, generation lengths, sampling-step budgets, evaluation procedures and schedule-selection subsets remain unchanged. Appendix E.6 also retains the same five-token, binary-vocabulary toy setup with three sampling steps.

E4.justification: Both versions retain the subset-versus-full-evaluation analysis in Table 1, schedule comparisons across synthetic distributions in Figure 4, and generated-output case studies in Tables 8–9. No ablation, robustness test or supplementary analysis changes.

E5.justification: The uncertainty entries and Appendix E.3's rule for highlighting results within ±1 standard deviation are unchanged. Neither version adds or revises run counts, seeds, confidence intervals or significance-testing procedures relative to the other.

E6.justification: Experimental figures and Tables 1–9 retain the same results. For example, Table 3's 64-step HumanEval scores remain 24.39 ± 3.36 for Beta(0.9,0.3) and 11.59 ± 2.51 for the linear schedule.

T1.justification: Section 2.1, Eq. (3), changes the masked-token probability from α_t to 1−α_t and the clean-token probability from 1−α_t to α_t. This corrects the conditional-flow definition to agree with α_0=0, α_1=1 and the existing derivations in Appendices C.1, D.2 and D.4. The theorem statements and appendix proofs remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same claims about energy equivalence, optimal scheduling, efficient Beta-CDF tuning and improved few-step sampling. No contribution or claim is strengthened, narrowed or added.

C2.justification: The interpretations of task-specific temporal preferences, near-optimal linear schedules on BBH/GSM8K, and the unresolved relationship between real-world tasks and optimal schedules remain unchanged, including the limitations and Appendix E.4.

D1.justification: Appendix E retains the same parameter-search guidance, LLaDA pretrained weights and evaluation toolkit, and single NVIDIA A800 GPU disclosure. Implementation details and code/data access information are unchanged.

R1.justification: The same 48 references and related-work discussion are retained, including the positioning relative to discrete flow matching and prior geodesic interpretations. The paper's own conference-status update does not revise its research positioning.

P1.justification: v2 expands author affiliations and funding acknowledgements and replaces the preprint notice with a NeurIPS 2025 conference notice. The scientific prose, section order and explanatory narrative otherwise remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Expanded front matter and acknowledgements cause text reflow and different page breaks, including moving the conclusion from page 9 to page 10. Figures 1–7 and Tables 1–9 retain their content and visual design.

improvement.justification: Correcting Eq. (3) resolves an internal inconsistency between the stated masked-to-clean time direction and the conditional probability definition, bringing the background into agreement with the existing appendix proofs. This provides a limited improvement in mathematical correctness and clarity; the method, empirical evidence and substantive conclusions remain unchanged.
